notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (PB5106 owns the group sibling, §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 GR2, and names no site). §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 GR1: "the numeric operand is treated as though it were moved to an elementary alphanumeric data item of the same size as the numeric data item (in terms of standard data format characters), and the content of this alphanumeric data item were then compared to the nonnumeric operand". RenderRelationalCore implements it, for every edition alike, as CobolString.Compare over OperandText.AsString(operand, deSign: true): the numeric operand's unsigned digit image, one character per digit position, compared under the program collating sequence with space extension of the shorter operand. That equals the 1985 result for an unsigned item, for an item with an embedded sign and for a SIGN SEPARATE item (the 1985 temporary is one character longer, a trailing space the shorter-operand extension supplies anyway), and a numeric literal compares as its digits. Probed at --std 85: 9(3) value 7 equals X(3) "007" and X(5) "007"; S9(3) value -7, embedded and TRAILING SEPARATE, equals "007" and "007 "; "007" = 007 is true and "007" = 7 is false; 9(3) > "006" is true. What is NOT implemented is the 1985 size of the temporary for a scaled integer: there is no edition arm. §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR8: "The scaling position character 'P' is not counted in the size of the data item", so a PIC 99PP item is 2 standard data format characters and the temporary is 2 characters long, while the move sends the four digits 1200 (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4: "all digit positions specified with this symbol are considered to have the value zero and are counted in the size of the sending operand"), which the alphanumeric receiver truncates on the right to "12". The compiler compares the four-character "1200", the 2023 temporary ("the same length in terms of character positions as the number of digits in the integer"), at 85 too. The row's change record names exactly this case as the 1985/2023 difference. The witness compares 9(3) and S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE items with literals and an X(4) item; it has no scaled operand.

next.reason: 1985: the numeric (integer, §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 'it must be an integer data item or an integer literal') operand 'is treated as though it were moved to an elementary alphanumeric data item of the same size as the numeric data item (in terms of standard data format characters)', then compared. 2023 keeps the pairing (§2023:8.8.4.2.1 GR6) and the move-then-compare scheme in §2023:8.8.4.2.5 (prose with no catalog rule id): 'treated as though it were moved, according to the rules of the MOVE statement, to an elementary data item of the same length in terms of character positions as the number of digits in the integer', of the class of the other operand (adding national). The temporary item's length basis changed from size in standard data format characters to the number of digits. A separate sign makes no observable difference (space extension), but for a scaled integer such as PIC 99PP, whose 'P' is 'not counted in the size of the item, but ... counted in the maximum number of digit positions' (§2023:13.18.40.4 GR14), 1985 truncates the moved value 1200 to a 2-character '12' while 2023 builds a 4-character '1200', so a comparison with '1200' changes truth value.
